# CoolDesk

> Don't open apps. Open spaces. Tabs, apps and files grouped into a space for each project. Free, open source, no sign-in.

CoolDesk is a free launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a new-tab extension for Chrome, Edge and Brave. It keeps your browser tabs, desktop apps, files and notes in spaces, one for each project, and Alt+K jumps back into any of them.

It is meant as a layer on top of the tools you already use (VS Code, GitHub, Figma, Linear, Notion, Slack…), not a replacement for them: each project gets a space that gathers the links, apps, folders and notes it needs, and one shortcut takes you back to it.

## Two pieces

### Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux)

- **Spotlight (Alt+K, changeable)** — one search across browser tabs, history, bookmarks, desktop apps, files and notes; picks an already-open tab or window instead of opening a duplicate
- **Slash commands** — `/new-workspace` creates a space, `/agent` hands a task to a local AI CLI (Claude Code, opencode, Codex), `/u` `/a` `/f` scope search to tabs, apps or files
- **Spaces** — one per project, each holding its links, editors, apps, folders and files, plus a status (Active / Planning / On Hold), a Next Up todo list and notes; anything already open is marked
- **File manager** — browse a space's folders, preview code, run project scripts, see which dev servers are up
- **Layouts** — full window, a sidebar or a bottom bar; sidebar and bar tuck away to a screen-edge handle and slide in over your work on hover (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+D to switch)

### Browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave)

- **New tab dashboard** — widgets, favorites, a resume card, your open tabs and what's playing, over a wallpaper
- **Works with the desktop app** — sends your open tabs to the desktop app over a local connection (127.0.0.1:4545), so Spotlight can find them and jump straight to one

## Privacy

Local-first: data stays on your device. The only things that leave it are an optional anonymous usage ping (can be turned off), cloud AI if you turn it on with your own key, and Team sync when you choose to share.

## Pricing

Free — no plans, no sign-in.

- [Home](https://cool-desk.com/)
- [How to Use](https://cool-desk.com/#how-to-use)
- [Widget Store](https://cool-desk.com/widgets) — free embeddable new-tab widgets: spotlight, project workspaces, session restore, daily focus, pomodoro, tasks, weather, habits, snippets, regex tester and more, plus support for adding your own custom widget
- [Blog](https://cool-desk.com/blog)
- [Under the hood](https://cool-desk.com/under-the-hood) — how CoolDesk works: the local WebSocket bridge between the extension and the Rust desktop app, search scoring and ranking, time tracking, file watching, sync and caching
- [Contact](https://cool-desk.com/contact)

## Comparisons

- [All comparisons](https://cool-desk.com/vs) — every CoolDesk comparison, grouped into launchers, tab managers and new tab pages
- [CoolDesk vs Workona](https://cool-desk.com/vs/workona) — cloud browser workspaces vs a free, local-first project workspace that includes desktop apps and files
- [CoolDesk vs Toby](https://cool-desk.com/vs/toby) — visual tab collections vs project workspaces with spotlight search across tabs, apps and notes
- [CoolDesk vs Raycast](https://cool-desk.com/vs/raycast) — a command palette vs a project-based launcher with browser-deep search
- [CoolDesk vs Alfred](https://cool-desk.com/vs/alfred) — the Mac classic vs a free launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux built around projects
- [CoolDesk vs Spotlight](https://cool-desk.com/vs/spotlight) — macOS's built-in launcher vs a free, project-based launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux
- [CoolDesk vs PowerToys Run](https://cool-desk.com/vs/powertoys) — Microsoft's free Windows launcher vs a free, project-based launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux
- [CoolDesk vs Momentum](https://cool-desk.com/vs/momentum) — a beautiful daily new-tab dashboard vs a project workspace with tabs, apps, notes and spotlight search
- [CoolDesk vs Flow Launcher](https://cool-desk.com/vs/flow-launcher) — the free open-source Windows launcher vs a free, project-based launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux with browser tabs built in
- [CoolDesk vs Arc](https://cool-desk.com/vs/arc) — Arc's browser Spaces vs project workspaces in the browser you already use, plus your apps, files and notes
- [CoolDesk vs OneTab](https://cool-desk.com/vs/onetab) — collapsing tabs into a list vs project workspaces you can search and reopen
- [CoolDesk vs Session Buddy](https://cool-desk.com/vs/session-buddy) — saving browser sessions vs saving whole projects — tabs, apps, files and notes
- [CoolDesk vs Chrome Tab Groups](https://cool-desk.com/vs/chrome-tab-groups) — Chrome's built-in tab groups vs AI-grouped project workspaces with one-keystroke search
